title: Scripture shows ordinary believers, not only especial saints, may be certain they are in grace
source_text: VIII. Neque vero putandum est id in sanctis illis viris fuisse peculiare, caeteros vero fideles, qui nullo singulari privilegio gaudent, non posse similiter apud se certo statuere an sint in Dei gratia, & beneficiorum nobis per Christum partorum revera participes. Nam multis modis ex Scriptura colligitur omnes qui Christo per veram vivamque fidem insiti sunt, absque ulla temeritate, certo ea de re posse concipere fiduciam & persuasionem. Primo enim Apostolus Rom. 8. docet fideles omnes accipere spiritum adoptionis, per quem Deum ut patrem agnoscunt & invocant, & spiritum Dei spiritui eorum testimonium perhibere quod sunt filii Dei, & Christi cohaeredes. Non enim accepistis, inquit, spiritum servitutis iterum in timore; sed Spiritum adoptionis filiorum, in quo clamamus Abba Pater. Ipse enim spiritus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro quod sumus filii Dei. Si autem filii, & haeredes; haeredes quidem Dei, cohaeredes autem Christi. Annon autem jure merito certi esse possumus de eo quod spiritus Dei nobis testatur suis in nobis motibus & effectis? Deinde Apostolus 2 Cor. 13. jubet Corinthios seipsos probare, an sint in fide; & explorare an Christus sit in ipsis. Quod frustra praeciperetur, nisi fidelis posset de seipso certo judicare. Denique Apostolus 1 Joan. 5. Haec scribo vobis, inquit, ut sciatis vos vitam aeternam habere, qui creditis in nomen Filii Dei. Unde manifestum est fideles posse certo scire se vitam aeternam habere, sibi esse remissa peccata, & nos per gratiam ejus renovatos in justitiam & sanctitatem veram, quae Deo grata atque accepta sit.
pass_a_gloss: Nor should it be thought that this was peculiar to those holy men, and that other believers who enjoy no singular privilege cannot likewise establish among themselves with certainty whether they are in God’s grace and truly share the benefits procured for us through Christ. For in many ways it is gathered from Scripture that all who are grafted into Christ by true and living faith can, without any rashness, conceive a certain confidence and persuasion of that matter. First the Apostle in Romans 8 teaches that all believers receive the Spirit of adoption by whom they acknowledge and call upon God as Father, and that God’s Spirit bears witness to their spirit that they are children of God and co-heirs with Christ. Next in 2 Corinthians 13 he bids the Corinthians prove themselves whether they are in the faith and examine whether Christ is in them—which would be enjoined in vain unless a believer could judge certainly of himself. Finally in 1 John 5 he writes so that they may know they have eternal life who believe in the name of the Son of God. From which it is plain that believers can certainly know they have eternal life, that their sins are remitted, and that through his grace they are renewed unto true righteousness and holiness pleasing and acceptable to God.
pass_b_english: Assurance is not a rare privilege of a few saints; Scripture gives it to all living believers.
Romans 8’s witness of the Spirit, self-examination in 2 Corinthians 13, and 1 John 5’s knowing eternal life show ordinary certainty is possible.
